title: A team clone deploys from the public copy: busy-host ceiling at setup, fetch-only upstream, local fixes and backlog provenance
goal: kb-setup asks the operator for the clone's test ceiling profile, usual or busy, where busy multiplies each platform's max_seconds by 15 in that clone only; an agent session cannot write the ceiling file or a decision row directly; the ceiling refusal names the route an operator in an IDE integrated terminal takes; kb-setup asks the deployment scope (me, team or org) and sets by it a fetch-only upstream remote that every push to it refuses; kbgit.py upstream brings the upstream main in by the scope's policy (me rebases, team or org merges) and lists each local commit changing an upstream-owned path; every backlog item records its provenance so a clone with an upstream shows only its own items unless asked for all; a GitHub issue template with a skill lets an agent write a clone's findings for upstream as user stories in one issue body; the maintainer turns such an issue back into draft backlog items that link it; kb_mcp.py registers the kb servers for a workspace directory above the clone with no hand-written .mcp.json

gates.question: Approve this sprint's goal and committed items?

notes: Goal widened 2026-10-19 by the operator in the planning session: deployment scope (me, team, org) chosen at setup with the fetch policy defined per scope; upstream backlog items kept, marked and hidden; findings travel back through a GitHub issue template an agent fills with user stories, which the maintainer converts to items; the ceiling profile stays a separate setup question.
